question: How much will Gold Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)

calls.reasoning: This is a two-week return spread; the drift is about zero and the dispersion is what matters. Gold vol in 2026 is extreme: there was a peak above $5,600 in January, the worst October since 2008, and a +3% day on Nov 4 after the midterms. That makes the GC-ES spread SD roughly 4.5-5.5pp over 10 trading days. The median is kept close to zero: dollar weakness after the midterms and lower yields favor gold, while hike pricing for the Dec Fed meeting (reportedly ~79%) and Iran-oil inflation pressure weigh on it. Fat tails leave a few percent probability beyond ±10. No human market was found (Polymarket/Manifold per harness; no Kalshi contract on this spread).

- Resolves off Yahoo Finance GC=F and ES=F daily closes. P0 = close on Fri Nov 6, 2026; P1 = close on Fri Nov 20, 2026. The value is GC% minus ES% in pp. Event window: Nov 9 -> Nov 20 (10 trading days); as of Nov 4 it is 0% elapsed, and P0 is not yet set.
- Gold rose ~2.6-3.4% on Nov 4, 2026 to ~$4,035-4,066, driven by a weaker USD (one-month low) and lower yields after Democrats swept the midterms (TradingEconomics, Nov 4).
- Gold is down ~9% YTD in 2026 and -1.8% over the past month. It hit an all-time high of ~$5,379-5,608 in Jan 2026 (TradingEconomics; Fortune Nov 2).
- Oct 2026 was gold's worst October since 2008: it closed at $3,875 after breaking support near $3,970. Fed meeting was Oct 27-28 (Yahoo Finance; goldsilver.com).
- A 10% rise in Brent since the Iran war began coincided with a 4% drop in gold; higher oil feeds expectations of further US rate hikes. Markets reportedly price ~79% odds of a December Fed hike (TradingEconomics).
- GVZ (gold implied vol) was ~22-24 in Sep-Oct 2026, with realized daily moves of 2-3% recently (search snippets).
- S&P 500 closed at 7,568.92 on Nov 3 (+0.36%), snapping a 3-day losing streak. ES futures fell ~0.6% after hours on the Democratic sweep (Yahoo/TheStreet, Nov 3).
- US gold ETFs took in $11.7B of inflows in Q3 2026 (SSGA/goldsilver).
- Dispersion: implied spread vol ≈ sqrt(gold vol^2 + ES vol^2 - 2*rho*...). With gold ~25%, ES ~16% and rho ~0.1, that is ~29% annualized, or ~5.8pp SD over 10 trading days. The 2025 biweekly GC-ES spreads in the Metaculus spreadsheet were typically within ±5pp (not re-verified this run).
- Status quo: the spread has roughly zero expected drift over two weeks.
- Searched but not found: an exact GVZ/VIX print for Nov 4, the Nov 6 closes, and any Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold market on this spread (none found).

calls.reasoning: This resolves as GC% minus ES% from the Nov 6 close to the Nov 20 close. A two-week return spread has essentially zero drift, so the median is near 0. A weaker USD after the midterms slightly favours gold; the ~79% December hike odds and Iran-oil inflation pressure offset that. Gold is in a high-volatility regime (worst October since 2008, +3% on Nov 4), which gives a spread SD of ~4.5-5pp. Fat tails leave ~2.5% outside each ±10pp bound. No human market was found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the resolution mechanics (P0 = Nov 6 close, P1 = Nov 20 close), on the market facts (gold ~$4,040, GVZ ~25, VIX ~21, ~79% December hike odds) and on a median near zero. The only dispute is how wide the distribution should be (10-90 widths of 10.7, 11.7 and 13). That is judgment: implied vol points to ~6pp SD and realized vol to ~4.7pp. I took a blended ~4.6pp SD, essentially carrying Run 1's width forward. I could not verify the Nov 6 P0 or the current GVZ level without web access. No human market was found by the harness or by any run.
